home.title: Home
paragraphs: This is the overview of your profile after sign-in.
Numbers and charts show how many jobs, courses, studies, and other details you have added. A fuller profile makes a better PDF CV.
Completeness points out what is still missing — contact info, photo, or professional summary.
Recent activity lists the latest changes so you can pick up where you left off.

settings.title: Profile
paragraphs: Name, contact details, photo, address, and the professional summary that opens your CV live here.
The summary can exist in more than one language — useful when your CV is read abroad.
In main skills, choose what to highlight and the order on your CV.
Download builds a PDF with your profile, jobs, studies, courses, projects, and skills, in the order you set.

skills.title: Skills
paragraphs: Plain words for what you know how to do at work, in study, or day to day.
Pick from the list or create a new one with the name you prefer.
They show on your profile and on jobs, courses, studies, and projects — showing where you use each one.
On your CV, profile skills can be grouped by category.

courses.title: Courses
paragraphs: Short courses, certificates, and training — for example a trade course, safety certification, or workshop.
Use this area for short-form learning. School, college, and technical programs belong in Education.
Add who ran it, the dates, a description, and related skills. Everything lands on your CV; relevance sets the prominence.

educations.title: Education
paragraphs: Formal studies: high school, technical programs, degrees, postgraduate work, and similar levels.
This is your main academic path. Short courses and certificates belong in Courses.
Add the institution, level, status, dates, and a description. You can link skills you gained.
On your CV, more relevant education entries get more prominence.

organizations.title: Organizations
paragraphs: Companies, schools, and institutions you name on your CV — where you worked, studied, or took a course.
Save each name once and reuse it on jobs, studies, and courses. If it is missing, create it with the correct name.
The name shows with every record that uses that organization.

projects.title: Projects
paragraphs: Work on your own or alongside a job: freelance, renovations, volunteering, or a deliverable you want to highlight beyond the job title.
Describe what you did, link skills that work shows, and add photos or links if you want.
Relevance sets how prominently each project appears on the PDF CV.

experiences.title: Experience
paragraphs: Jobs and work in your history — each one linked to a company or client.
Within the same experience you can record more than one role, useful when you changed title without changing employer.
Each role has a title, dates, description, and skills used in that job.
Also set the job type and how important that job is on your CV.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
paragraphs: Use these when another system needs to read or update your data on its own, without opening this site.
Common with apps, scripts, or tools that sync your profile.
Give each token a name you will recognize in the list — for example the system that will use it.
When creating one, choose whether it can only read data or also change it. The secret appears once: store it safely and revoke what you no longer need.
